newsitem.title: UK: Nobel prize important signal to Jakarta - Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Nobel prize important signal to Jakarta - Amnesty.

text.p: The award of the Nobel Peace Prize to Bishop Carlos Felipe Belo and Jose Ramos-Horta was an important signal of international concern about human rights in East Timor that should be heeded by Indonesia, Amnesty International said on Friday.
The human rights watchdog, itself awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977, said this year's award would help bring East Timor back into the international spotlight.
"Bishop Belo and Jose Ramos Horta have won this prize for their efforts to find a peaceful, political settlement to the East Timor issue," Amnesty International said in a statement.
"We shouldn't forget that countless numbers of their fellow East Timorese have been killed, tortured or gaoled for the same thing. The human rights situation in East Timor remains extremely grave."
Amnesty said disappearances and political killings remained uninvestigated and unresolved.
A long-term solution to the East Timor issue cannot be found without tackling human rights violations at their root cause -- repression by the Indonesian government and military, it said.
"The international community must watch developments closely over coming days to ensure there is no new crackdown," said Amnesty.
